messages.author: 51f922b950bae924
messages.subject: Error in categorical CFA model comparison
parts:
Hi,
I have a dataset (attached) where some of the indicators are categorical.
I fit two models, but when I compare their fit (with anova, see attached commands) I get the following error:
Error in P1 + (t(Delta1[[g]]) %*% WLS.V[[g]] %*% Delta1[[g]]) :
  non-conformable arrays

Can you help me with that?
Thanks
Yigal

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Error in categorical CFA model comparison
parts:
On 08/12/2013 07:23 PM, Yigal Attali wrote:
> Hi,
> I have a dataset (attached) where some of the indicators are categorical.
> I fit two models, but when I compare their fit (with anova, see attached
> commands) I get the following error:
> Error in P1 + (t(Delta1[[g]]) %*% WLS.V[[g]] %*% Delta1[[g]]) :
> non-conformable arrays

I agree that the error message is rather cryptic, but the anova()
function only deals with models that are *nested* in each other, in the
strict sense: the restricted model should be a subset of the
unrestricted model... This is not the case for a 1-factor model versus a
2-factor model.

I tried to write code that would check for this, but I have not found a
satisfactory solution (yet).

Yves.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Error in categorical CFA model comparison
parts:
Yigal,
As a work-around, you could compare the two factor model with the
covariance between factors freely estimated to the same model with the
covariance fixed to unity. Fix the scale using the factor variances
rather than a fixed loading so that the covariance can be positive even
if the polarity of the items is opposite. This was common practice
before it was commonly understood that models could be nested even if
their parameters were not nested.

Keith
